name: Vancomycin
summary: IV glycopeptide for serious Gram-positive (esp. MRSA) infections; oral form (not absorbed) treats C. difficile colitis.
mechanism: Binds D-Ala-D-Ala precursors of peptidoglycan and blocks cell-wall synthesis at an earlier step than beta-lactams.
pharmacodynamics: Time-dependent killing; AUC24/MIC (or trough) guided dosing.

dosing.adult: IV: 15-20 mg/kg every 8-12 hours (trough/AUC-guided); oral: 125 mg every 6 hours for C. difficile colitis
dosing.renalAdjustment: Yes — dose and interval adjusted to renal function and levels

safety.lactation: Compatible — negligible absorption in nursing infant
warnings: Red man syndrome (infusion-rate related histamine release — not an allergy)

clinicalPearls: Oral vancomycin is NOT absorbed — IV for systemic infections, oral only for C. difficile
AUC-guided dosing is preferred over trough-only in serious infections
good: Standard therapy for invasive MRSA and oral therapy for C. difficile.
bad: Nephrotoxicity (especially with piperacillin-tazobactam), slow bactericidal activity, and no activity against VRE.
